title: Two papers disagree (diet-and-mortality)
explanation: Claim A asserts a J-shaped curvilinear dose-response relationship between alcohol consumption and stroke risk, whereas Claim B asserts a linear relationship where higher consumption is consistently associated with higher risk.
a_text: Alcohol consumption exhibits a curvilinear J-shaped dose-response relationship with the relative risk of ischemic stroke.
b_text: Higher alcohol consumption is roughly linearly associated with a higher risk of stroke (HR 1.14 per 100 g/week higher consumption).

audit.reason: Both meta-analyses on comparable populations; the disagreement is model choice (fractional-polynomial J-shape vs assumed linear). A modelling-choice disagreement on the same construct is a substantive disagreement.
audit.basis: builder's hand review against the source abstracts (venue, method, population, dose, outcome)
